title: Quantum-assisted rendezvous on hypercubes: a quantum Bernoulli noise approach
abstract: We study quantum-assisted balanced rendezvous on the $d$-dimensional hypercube in a one-step two-agent quantum-walk framework, where the two agents move the same Hamming distance and meet at a common midpoint. The key structure is a projective $t$-sphere resolution, which governs exact finite-dimensional quantum attainment. Its scalar analogue recovers the corresponding classical characterization. We characterize finite-dimensional quantum attainment of the no-signalling benchmark, construct quantum strategies from projective sphere resolutions, and establish a rigidity theorem for optimal finite-dimensional strategies. A marked difference appears between nearest-neighbor and higher-cardinality updates: quantum advantage can occur in the former, whereas in the latter the geometry of the relevant Hamming spheres rules out exact finite-dimensional attainment of the no-signalling value. Together, these results connect quantum-walk dynamics, Hamming-sphere geometry, and quantum rendezvous within the quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN) framework.
summary: This work analyzes quantum-assisted rendezvous on the hypercube using the Quantum Bernoulli Noises framework. It establishes that the ability to reach the no-signalling bound depends critically on the update step size $t$ relative to the dimension $d$. The findings reveal a structural breakdown of quantum advantage for larger step sizes, linking quantum walk dynamics directly to Hamming-sphere geometry.
main_problem: The paper characterizes the conditions under which quantum strategies can achieve the no-signalling bound in a rendezvous game played on the hypercube.
main_result: Quantum advantage exists for nearest-neighbor updates ($t=1$) when $d$ is not a power of two, but for higher cardinality updates ($t \ge 2$) and $d > 2t$, the geometry of the Hamming spheres prevents achieving the no-signalling bound.
method: The analysis uses the Quantum Bernoulli Noises (QBN) framework to model the two-agent quantum walk and establishes mathematical equivalences between quantum attainment, the existence of projective $t$-sphere resolutions, and compatible coin fields.
model_or_system: The system is a two-agent quantum walk on the $d$-dimensional hypercube ($\Gamma^d$). The process is governed by local quantum updates implemented via the QBN approach, comparing classical, quantum, and no-signalling bounds.
key_observables: The success probability of the rendezvous, $\omega_{d,t}(P)$, and the no-signalling bound, $\omega_{NS}(d, t)$.
important_parameters: Dimension $d$ of the hypercube, and the update cardinality $t$ ($1 \le t \le d/2$).
main_assumptions: The results focus on exact finite-dimensional quantum attainment, not asymptotic limits, and rely on the existence of specific projective $t$-sphere resolutions.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the rendezvous problem and the QBN model, establishing the no-signalling bound, proving the equivalence between quantum attainment and the existence of projective $t$-sphere resolutions, and finally analyzing the specific cases of $t=1$ versus $t \ge 2$ to characterize quantum advantage.
why_interesting: The connection between geometric structures (Hamming spheres) and fundamental quantum information bounds (no-signalling) provides deep insights into the limits of quantum correlations in discrete state spaces, which is relevant for quantum communication protocols.
